assumptions: Use the standard Dolev-Yao adversarial network model.
Model only the protocol behavior described by the current IR and modeling contract.
Do not use the reference Sapic+ or Tamarin models during generation; they are evaluation metadata only.

fresh_terms.name: ~Na
fresh_terms.purpose: nonce generated freshly by initiator A

fresh_terms.name: ~Nb
fresh_terms.purpose: nonce generated freshly by responder B

long_term_keys.name: skA
long_term_keys.policy: private setup/state for honest A; reveal only via explicit Reveal(A, skA) if modeled

long_term_keys.name: skB
long_term_keys.policy: private setup/state for honest B; reveal only via explicit Reveal(B, skB) if modeled

long_term_keys.name: skC
long_term_keys.policy: private setup/state for honest C; if C is instantiated as an adversary-controlled principal, the adversary may know skC by ownership rather than by an honest-key reveal

messages.label: M1
messages.meaning: Initiator A sends identity A and freshly generated nonce Na encrypted under the public key of intended responder B.

messages.label: M2
messages.meaning: Responder B decrypts M1, treats the identity field A_M1 as Alice, echoes the received nonce Na_M1, adds freshly generated nonce Nb, and encrypts the pair under pub(A_M1). In the honest diagram A_M1 is A.

messages.label: M3
messages.meaning: Initiator A decrypts M2, checks the echoed nonce against its generated Na, and sends the received nonce Nb encrypted under the public key of its locally intended peer B.

checks: check Na_M2 == ~Na generated by this A session
check Nb_M3 == ~Nb generated by this B session

checks.condition: decrypt M1 using B's private key skB and parse the plaintext as <A_M1, Na_M1>
decrypt M2 using A's private key skA, parse the plaintext as <Na_M2, Nb_M2>, and check Na_M2 equals A's previously generated ~Na
decrypt M3 using B's private key skB, parse the plaintext as Nb_M3, and check Nb_M3 equals B's previously generated ~Nb

events.name: Start_A
events.when: A generates Na and sends M1 to its intended peer B

events.name: Secret
events.when: A generates Na for a run intended with B

events.name: Running_B
events.when: B has decrypted M1, generated Nb, and sends M2 using the identity A_M1 obtained from M1

events.name: Secret
events.when: B generates Nb for the peer identity A_M1 extracted from M1

events.name: Commit_A
events.when: A decrypts M2, verifies the echoed Na, and sends M3 to its locally intended peer B

events.name: Commit_B
events.when: B decrypts M3 and verifies the returned Nb

claims.intent: Typing/source discipline for values parsed from encrypted messages and local state in the NSPK role rules.
claims.witness: All message variables used in events are generated locally, received from the network, or obtained by successful decryption and parsing as described by the role actions.

claims.intent: Secrecy of nonces marked by Secret events for initiator and responder sessions of the described, unfixed Needham-Schroeder public-key protocol.
claims.witness: Expected counterexample metadata is preserved. The parsed protocol intentionally contains no responder identity in M2 and no Lowe fix; public keys for arbitrary agents are available.

claims.intent: Injective agreement between initiator and responder on peer identities and nonces for completed runs.
claims.witness: Expected authentication counterexample metadata is preserved. The protocol lacks B's identity in M2, so A's peer identity at Commit_A is local state rather than cryptographic evidence from M2.

claims.intent: Existence of an executable trace in which the protocol exchange completes. The natural-language protocol defines nonce exchange only and does not define a derived session key.
claims.witness: Honest trace: A sends M1, B decrypts M1 and sends M2, A decrypts M2 and checks Na, A sends M3, and B decrypts M3 and checks Nb.

compromise.policy: No explicit reveal or corruption events are described in the natural-language protocol or supplied goals. Honest private keys remain setup/state secrets unless a later modeling contract adds explicit Reveal events. The Dolev-Yao adversary controls the network and knows all public keys pub(C); if adversary-controlled principals are modeled, their own private keys are adversary-known by ownership and not treated as reveals of honest principals.

abstractions: A and B are schematic protocol roles and identities from the message diagram; public-key lookup pub(C) is retained for arbitrary agent identities C as stated in the initial knowledge.
The network is adversarial: messages may be intercepted, replayed, redirected, and composed by the Dolev-Yao adversary.
No explicit message tags are present in the source protocol; none are added.
No responder identity B is included inside M2; this is preserved and not repaired with the Lowe fix.
No session-key derivation is described; the session_key_setup_possible goal is represented as reachability of protocol completion events rather than by inventing a new key.
modeling_assumptions: Each role instance stores its local intended peer identity: A uses local B when choosing pub(B) for M1 and M3.
Responder B uses the identity field decrypted from M1, written A_M1, to select pub(A_M1) for M2.
The notation pub(X) denotes the public key corresponding to X's private key.
The parser preserves supplied expected results as review metadata; they are not used to strengthen or repair the protocol.
The protocol has no explicit key confirmation beyond A's check of Na in M2 and B's check of Nb in M3.

semantic_constraints.policy: M1 plaintext is exactly the pair <A, Na>; it does not include B's identity or any signature.
M2 plaintext is exactly the pair <Na, Nb>; it does not include A's identity, B's identity, a signature, or a tag.
M3 plaintext is exactly Nb; it does not include A's identity, B's identity, Na, a signature, or a tag.
A's check after receiving M2 is equality of the echoed Na with the locally generated Na; A obtains no cryptographic evidence from M2 that B generated Nb.
B's check after receiving M3 is equality of the returned Nb with the locally generated Nb; B relies on the identity A_M1 from M1 as the peer identity.
Do not add the Lowe fix message aenc(<Na, Nb, B>, pub(A)) or any equivalent responder-identity binding unless a later contract explicitly changes the protocol.
